subject: principles-of-accounts
title: Double Entry: One Purchase, Two Accounts

segments.say: Opening position: the equation balances. The business opens with $10,000 cash, provided by the owner as capital, and owes nothing, so assets of $10,000 equal capital of $10,000 plus liabilities of $0. Point at the three boxes on your student notes diagram before any purchase is made.
questions: What does the business hold at the opening position, and who provided it?
Why does the equation balance before anything is bought?

segments.say: The purchase: cash flows out, equipment arrives. The business pays $4,000 cash for equipment, and the payment and the arrival happen in the same single transaction. Now try the purchase questions on your worksheet.
questions: What leaves the business in this transaction, and what arrives?
Is the purchase one transaction or two separate events, and why does it matter?

segments.say: Both accounts change by the same $4,000. The cash account falls by $4,000 to $6,000 and the equipment account rises by $4,000 to $4,000 at the same moment. Check the two account balances against your student notes before moving on.
questions: Which two accounts change, and by how much does each change?
What is the total of the two asset balances after both changes?

segments.say: Re-checked: the equation still balances. Total assets are $6,000 cash plus $4,000 equipment, still $10,000, and Assets = Capital + Liabilities still balances. Keep the opening, purchase, both-changes, re-checked order as you check your student notes and finish the exit ticket.
questions: How do you prove the equation still balances after the purchase?
What are the four stages of the double-entry recording, in order?
segments.watchFor: Buying equipment with cash makes the business poorer so total assets fall. Listen for students who look only at the cash leaving and conclude the business has lost value. Send them back to scene 3 and the two accounts changing together: One asset is swapped for another of equal value, so total assets and the equation are unchanged. Paying $4,000 cash for equipment cuts the cash asset by $4,000 and raises the equipment asset by $4,000 at the same moment, total assets stay at $10,000, and Assets = Capital + Liabilities stays balanced - every transaction is recorded twice, once in each account it changes.
